title: Vesper and the Wolf
premise: Silas Fairweather, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Vesper Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When prayers begin reaching the old gods again, each answered wish leaves a wound in the world's memory, and Silas discovers her own forgotten past is the key: she once broke her oath and killed a god to end the ancient war. As the moon nears its thirteenth turn, she must choose between revealing that secret—which would reignite the war—or letting the gods' returning power consume the city. In the end, Silas sacrifices her remaining memories of everyone she loves to seal the gods away again, paying the final price of survival.
about_author: Odile Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken oaths in municipal records before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog arrives earlier every year, and swears this is coincidence.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Silas. In the Vesper Guild's counting house, Silas appraises a vial of bottled grief and balances the guild's ledgers, establishing her precision, her hidden swordspeaker scars, and her rule against asking where goods come from. When a client prays aloud over a stolen relic—and something answers—the chapter ends with the ledger ink turning black on its own. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The Guildmaster orders Silas to investigate the answered prayer before the guild's clients panic. She consults an exiled astronomer who reveals the moon will complete its thirteenth turn—a cycle that last coincided with the Godswar. Silas recognizes the date from a memory that isn't hers. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren, a street thief whose dying sister was healed by a prayer to the old god Vaul—the first miracle in three centuries. Wren owes Vaul everything and becomes his willing messenger, showing the seductive side of returned divinity. She crosses paths with Silas while stealing a guild relic. Emotional beat: desperate gratitude curdling toward fanaticism.

chapters.title: The Oath That Was Broken
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Following the black-ink trail, Silas finds a shrine defaced with her own handwriting in a language she shouldn't know. A fragmentary vision surfaces: a battlefield, a god begging, her blade falling. Her oath-scar burns for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: horror at a self she cannot remember being.

chapters.title: Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Vaul's miracles spread through the lower city, but each healed person forgets someone they love; Wren's sister no longer remembers her. When Wren protests, Vaul shows her a vision of the Godswar—gods slaughtered by swordspeakers—and casts Silas as the butcher. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into hatred.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Price
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The Guildmaster reveals the guild has been trading with the waking gods for years, selling memories as offerings, and offers Silas a bargain: her forgotten past in exchange for neutrality. Refusing, she learns the guild built its fortune on the war's aftermath. Emotional beat: betrayal, and resolve hardened by it.

chapters.title: Where Prayers Go to Die
chapters.summary: POV Silas and Wren in alternating sections. Silas descends into the drowned temple beneath the city seeking proof of what really ended the war; Wren, sent to kill her, instead witnesses the truth in the temple's living murals: the gods demanded human memory as tribute, and Silas's broken oath saved millions. Emotional beat: collision of enemies becoming reluctant allies.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The moon completes its turn; Vaul achieves full manifestation and begins reclaiming all memories ever traded through the guild, unraveling thousands of minds at once. Wren must choose between the god who healed her sister and the sister herself, who begs Wren to stop him. Emotional beat: loyalty breaking and remaking itself.

chapters.title: Swordspeak
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the guild's counting house-turned-altar, Silas speaks her oath aloud for the first time since the war, her voice unbinding the god's hold on the city's stolen memories. She confronts Vaul with the truth he buried: he begged her to kill him, corrupted beyond saving. The climax hinges on whether she can do it twice. Emotional beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Empty Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas seals the gods away by offering the one payment they cannot refuse: every memory she has of the people she loves, including Wren. The city wakes whole; Wren remembers everything and mourns a friend who now looks at her kindly and without recognition. Silas returns to her ledgers, blank pages waiting. Emotional beat: sorrowful, hard-won peace.
